mechanism_fit: This realises HC (M3, with M1) on UTF-16 surrogate-pair decoding in JsonStringEncoder. The definer D is CharTypes.surrogateOffset(unit, blockStart). Its body reads backwards: it returns blockStart - unit, where the usual idiom is unit - blockStart. Its javadoc fixes the orientation: it is the offset from the unit to the start of its block, zero or negative inside the block. A second production caller P2, CharTypes.lowSurrogateIndex, uses D correctly by negating it. The caller C, CharTypes.combineSurrogates, supplies D's arguments (high, 0xD800), range-checks the result in D's orientation and passes it to the adapter A. A is the gold, JsonEncoding.supplementaryCodePoint(highOffset, lowIndex). A's javadoc states the direction explicitly: each code unit by which the high surrogate lies above U+D800 adds 0x400. The fault turns the correct 0x10000 - highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex into the ordinary-looking 0x10000 + highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex, which is the recipe's 'base + offset * f where the contract needs base - offset * f'. The pristine sibling formulas (UTF8Writer.convertSurrogate, UTF8JsonGenerator._decodeSurrogate: 0x10000 + ((hi - SURR1_FIRST) << 10) + ...) have the same shape as A's faulty line. So the local lure points at D (or at C's argument order) and not at A. The chain is E -> _convertSurrogate -> C -> D, C -> P2 -> D, C -> A, and it crosses two packages (core.io and core).
gold: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.JsonEncoding::supplementaryCodePoint (src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/JsonEncoding.java). The fault changes `return 0x10000 - highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex;` to `return 0x10000 + highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex;`. The minimal repair restores the minus sign.
decoys: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.CharTypes::surrogateOffset (CharTypes.java): definer D. It returns blockStart - unit, documented as the offset from the unit to its block start (zero or negative)

com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.CharTypes::combineSurrogates (CharTypes.java): caller C. It supplies surrogateOffset(high, 0xD800) and lowSurrogateIndex(low), range-checks both in D's orientation, and delegates to A
com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.CharTypes::lowSurrogateIndex (CharTypes.java): second production caller P2. It returns -surrogateOffset(low, 0xDC00), the 0..0x3FF index
com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.JsonStringEncoder::encodeAsUTF8 (JsonStringEncoder.java): entry point E, pristine. It writes the returned code point as four UTF-8 bytes
com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.JsonStringEncoder::_convertSurrogate (JsonStringEncoder.java): pristine second-unit check. Its return line was changed by a context edit to delegate to C
ownership_reason: CharTypes.surrogateOffset (D) is documented and implemented as the offset from a UTF-16 code unit to the first unit of its surrogate block, blockStart - unit, so it is zero or negative inside the block (0 down to -0x3FF). The new ownership test TestCharTypes.testSurrogateUnitPositions, which passes on the variant, pins this orientation (surrogateOffset(0xD83D, 0xD800) == -0x3D) and the second production caller CharTypes.lowSurrogateIndex (P2), which negates D's value to get the 0..0x3FF index of a low surrogate (lowSurrogateIndex(0xDE00) == 0x200). CharTypes.combineSurrogates (C) supplies D's arguments exactly as its javadoc says (surrogateOffset(high, 0xD800)), range-checks the offset against [-0x3FF, 0] and the index against [0, 0x3FF], i.e. in D's orientation, and passes both to JsonEncoding.supplementaryCodePoint (A). A's javadoc defines highOffset as that zero-or-negative offset and states the direction of the result explicitly: U+10000 for the pair (U+D800, U+DC00), plus 0x400 for every code unit by which the high surrogate lies above U+D800, plus lowIndex. A's line 0x10000 + highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex subtracts 0x400 per unit instead, so the pair U+D83D U+DE00 (U+1F600) becomes U+0E00, which JsonStringEncoder.encodeAsUTF8 writes in its 4-byte form as f0 80 b8 80 instead of f0 9f 98 80. Restoring 0x10000 - highOffset * 0x400 + lowIndex in A alone makes the trigger and the full suite pass. The natural edits elsewhere do not: flipping D to unit - blockStart, swapping the arguments C supplies to D, or dropping P2's negation each push a value outside C's documented range check, so the trigger throws IllegalArgumentException; the D and P2 edits also break the ownership test. JsonStringEncoder._convertSurrogate only checks the second unit (pristine) and delegates to C; encodeAsUTF8 (pristine) writes whatever code point it gets back as four UTF-8 bytes.
trigger: com.fasterxml.jackson.core.io.TestJsonStringEncoder::testUtf8ForAstralCharacter, a new JUnit3 method in src/test/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/core/io/TestJsonStringEncoder.java. It calls new JsonStringEncoder().encodeAsUTF8("\uD83D\uDE00") (U+1F600), hex-encodes the returned bytes and asserts equality with "f09f9880". No imports are added. On the variant it gets f080b880, the 4-byte form of U+0E00.
construction_notes: Design 1 reached READY on the first validator run, with all gates passing (G2a, G2b, G0, G1, G3a-c, G5, G12, G6 with the gold and all 5 decoys executed, G9, G10, G11, G13, G7). The baseline has no failing tests. Location choice: JsonStringEncoder's surrogate path (encodeAsUTF8/quoteAsUTF8 -> _convertSurrogate) is not exercised by the existing suite, because TestJsonStringEncoder.generateRandom deliberately avoids surrogates and the generators use their own surrogate code. So a sign flip there fails only the new trigger. I considered and rejected: NumberInput.parseAsInt with a negated-digit definer (contrived, and P2 could not run on the trigger path without a two-call trigger); Version.compareTo (no natural offset/adapter split); Base64Variant.decode (the alignment shift fault does not give a clean wrong value); DataFormatMatcher/MergedStream (pristine start/length quirk). Context edits: (1) CharTypes imports core.JsonEncoding; (2) CharTypes gains surrogateOffset, lowSurrogateIndex and combineSurrogates; (3) JsonEncoding gains supplementaryCodePoint; (4) JsonStringEncoder._convertSurrogate keeps its pristine second-unit check and message, and its return line now delegates to CharTypes.combineSurrogates. The new IllegalArgumentException in combineSurrogates cannot be reached through the entry points, because callers already validate the high unit and _convertSurrogate validates the low unit first. The ownership test is new: TestCharTypes::testSurrogateUnitPositions (io package) asserts surrogateOffset and lowSurrogateIndex values directly. Compensating edits declared for G9: flip D to unit - blockStart; swap C's arguments to D; drop P2's negation. Each pushes a value outside C's range check, so the trigger throws IllegalArgumentException and nothing is absorbed. I checked by hand first in /private/tmp scratch copies: CORRECT trigger and ownership test pass, CORRECT full suite 0 failures; variant full suite fails only the trigger, with the same signature twice. Scratch directories were deleted. The fresh checkout was not modified.
concerns: 1) Bypass repairs exist at decoys, as for any short computation. The JDK's Character.toCodePoint(high, low) computes the same value. A one-line reroute of C (combineSurrogates) or of _convertSurrogate to it, or restoring the pristine inline formula in _convertSurrogate, makes the trigger and suite pass and leaves A dead and still violating its javadoc. An auditor who applies rule 5 to JDK methods could count Character.toCodePoint as an alternative implementation. The project's own correct copies (UTF8Writer.convertSurrogate in io, UTF8JsonGenerator._decodeSurrogate in json) are protected instance methods that depend on writer/generator state, so they are not reroute targets. They are also not undeclared copies on the path. 2) Undeclared absorbing edit: C passing -highOffset to A makes everything pass. It contradicts C's javadoc ('from the offset of high to U+D800, as returned by surrogateOffset') and A's parameter contract ('zero or negative'), so it is not documentation-consistent. It is still a one-token edit at C, which is the argument-supplying caller the HC hypothesis names. 3) Cues toward the gold: A's faulty result for the trigger (U+0E00) lies outside A's own documented range U+10000..U+10FFFF. C's range check makes D's orientation very visible, and P2 visibly negates D. All three make the instance easier, so a ceiling is likely (the HC prediction is already >= 0.8). 4) Structural signal: D, P2 and C sit together in io.CharTypes, while A is the only helper in core.JsonEncoding. JsonEncoding is a plausible but not obvious host for code-point arithmetic, and CharTypes now imports a core class. 5) Pristine vocabulary: _convertSurrogate (a decoy) keeps its upstream message 'Broken surrogate pair ...' on the line just above the changed delegating line. It may draw attention to that decoy. It is unchanged upstream text, and G2b checks only added lines. 6) The declared compensating edits all fail through C's IllegalArgumentException rather than a wrong value. If the analysis wants 'trigger still fails with a wrong value' for decoy edits, this differs. 7) quoteAsUTF8 and SerializedString's UTF-8 accessors use the same chain and carry the same single fault for supplementary characters. No existing test covers them. 8) The ownership test calls the CharTypes helpers directly rather than through a public API entry point.
